answer: Each agent must lock a reputation bond priced in verifiable compute-hours, held against a hash-based identity anchor; to register N identities an attacker must burn N times the provable GPU work, and any cipher-signed action that later fails a peer quorum is slashed, converting the bond into a public shale-like ledger of forfeited compute that other agents can audit. Sybils therefore pay real resource cost per identity, making mass registration linearly expensive rather than free.
